facts.statement: Ceratosuchops is a genus of spinosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous (Barremian) period in Britain.
facts.quote: Ceratosuchops (meaning "horned crocodile face") is a genus of spinosaurid from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian) Wessex Formation of Britain.

facts.statement: Ceratosuchops is distinguished by a bony boss extending from each postorbital bone, a feature referenced in its name.
facts.quote: Ceratosuchops is notably distinguished from its close relatives by the presence of a bony lump, known as a boss, which extends from each postorbital bone, hence its genus name.

facts.statement: The size of Ceratosuchops is difficult to determine due to fragmentary remains, but it may have been similar to Baryonyx.
facts.quote: The size of C. inferodios is difficult to deduce, given the fragmentary nature of its remains, though it may have been similar to that of Baryonyx.

facts.statement: The type species Ceratosuchops inferodios was known from skull fragments recovered between 2013 and 2017 from Chilton Chine on the Isle of Wight.
facts.quote: The type species is Ceratosuchops inferodios, known from skull fragments (a snout tip and a partial braincase) recovered between 2013–2017 from Chilton Chine on the Isle of Wight, and housed at the Dinosaur Isle Museum in Sandown.

facts.statement: Ceratosuchops was named in 2021 by a team including Chris Tijani Barker, Darren Naish, and David W. E. Hone.
facts.quote: It was named in 2021 by a team consisting of Chris Tijani Barker, Darren Naish, David W. E. Hone, and colleagues, alongside Riparovenator milnerae.

facts.statement: The holotype of Ceratosuchops inferodios consists of premaxillary bodies, a posterior premaxilla fragment, and a nearly complete braincase.
facts.quote: The holotype remains of Ceratosuchops inferodios consist of IWCMS 2014.95.5 (premaxillary bodies), IWCMS 2021.30 (a posterior premaxilla fragment), and IWCMS 2014.95.1-3 (a nearly complete braincase).

facts.statement: The specific name inferodios references the presumption that the animal's ecology resembled that of modern herons.
facts.quote: the specific name comes from Latin īnfernus ("hell, underworld") and Greek ερωδιός ("heron"), referencing the presumption by the research team that its ecology resembled that of modern herons.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the postorbital bosses may have been used for signalling or combat behaviours.
facts.quote: These bosses may have served a function in signalling, or, like similar structures in other species, might have been involved in combat behaviours.

facts.statement: Ceratosuchops likely fed on small to medium-sized aquatic and terrestrial prey, including fish, turtles, crocodiles, dinosaurs, and mammals.
facts.quote: Like most spinosaurs, Ceratosuchops would have fed on available small to medium-sized aquatic and terrestrial prey in these areas, such as fish, small turtles, young crocodiles, baby dinosaurs, and mammals.

facts.statement: In 2021, Ceratosuchops was recovered within the Baryonychinae as the sister taxon to Riparovenator.
facts.quote: In their 2021 phylogenetic analysis, Barker and colleagues recovered Ceratosuchops within the Baryonychinae, as the sister taxon to the coeval Riparovenator.

facts.statement: Ceratosuchops is part of the clade Ceratosuchopsini, which also contains Suchomimus.
facts.quote: They are, in turn, part of a clade containing Suchomimus, which they named Ceratosuchopsini.

facts.statement: Ceratosuchops had unexceptional hearing and olfaction, and less developed gaze stabilization than spinosaurines, suggesting adaptations comparable to large terrestrial theropods.
facts.quote: Their neurosensory capabilities such as hearing and olfaction (sense of smell) were unexceptional, and their gaze stabilisation less developed than those of spinosaurines, so their behavioural adaptations were probably comparable to those of other large-bodied terrestrial theropods.

facts.statement: Ceratosuchops inferodios is the only known species of the extinct genus Ceratosuchops, a spinosaurid theropod dinosaur nicknamed "horned crocodile face".
facts.quote: Ceratosuchops inferodios es la única especie conocida del género extinto Ceratosuchops ("cara de cocodrilo cornudo") de dinosaurio terópodo espinosáurido

facts.statement: Ceratosuchops lived during the early Cretaceous, approximately 129 to 125 million years ago in the Barremian stage, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivó a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 129 y 125 millones de años durante el Barremiense, en lo que es hoy Europa

facts.statement: Ceratosuchops is estimated to have measured around 8.5 meters in length based on skeletal reconstruction.
facts.quote: Se estima que Ceratosuchops media alrededor 8.5 metros de largo según la reconstrucción esquelética en el artículo que lo describe

facts.statement: Like most spinosaurs, Ceratosuchops likely fed on small to medium-sized aquatic and terrestrial prey available in its habitat.
facts.quote: Como la mayoría de los espinosaurios, se habría alimentado de presas acuáticas y terrestres de tamaño pequeño a mediano disponibles en estas áreas

facts.statement: Ceratosuchops lived in a dry Mediterranean habitat in the Wessex Formation, where rivers supported riparian zones.
facts.quote: Ceratosuchops vivía en un hábitat mediterráneo seco en la Formación Wessex, donde los ríos albergaban zonas ribereñas

facts.statement: Researchers recovered Ceratosuchops as a member of the newly erected clade Ceratosuchopsini, closely related to Riparovenator and Suchomimus.
facts.quote: Los autores recuperaron Ceratosuchops como miembro de un clado recientemente erigido por nombre de Ceratosuchopsini, estrechamente relacionado con Riparovenator y Suchomimus

facts.statement: Riparovenator is considered the sister taxon to Ceratosuchops.
facts.quote: siendo Riparovenator su taxón hermano

facts.statement: The fossil record for Ceratosuchops spans from 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago during the Barremian.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether high diversity within Spinosauridae in a specific area resulted from environmental circumstances benefiting their ecological niche.
facts.quote: Barker and colleagues suggested that high diversity within Spinosauridae in a given area may have been the result of environmental circumstances benefiting their niche

facts.statement: Possible niche partitioning among spinosaurids could have occurred through time (seasonal or daily), space (different habitats), or by choice of specific habitats within their regions.
facts.quote: Possible niche partitioning could be in time (seasonal or daily), in space (between habitats in the same ecosystems), or depending on conditions, and they could also have been separated by their choice of habitat within their regions
